1| This course covers topics such as searching and reviewing the literature, identifying a research
1| problem, research ethics, research questions and objectives, types of research, designing a
1| methodology, methods of data collection and analysis using statistical tools, interpretation of
1| data, and drawing conclusions.
1| 901702 Engineering Project Management and Sustainability
1| This course provides understanding of financial, social and environmental sustainable
1| practices in project management to ensure that organization can continue to operate,
1| regardless of obstacles such as resource shortages, environmental disasters, legal
1| requirements, and social and political events. The course will also describe the impact of
1| sustainability requirements on the cost and schedule of projects. This course also covers the
1| trends in green design and implementation, circular economy, and the various rating Systems
1| and certification, and scopes of emissions.
1| 901703 Advanced Engineering Economy
1| The course topics will cover: analysis of capital investments in engineering projects, decision
1| analysis methods, cash flows, revenue requirements, replacement analysis, taz impact,
1| depreciation, activity-based analysis, multi-attribute decisions, probabilistic analysis and
1| sensitivity/risk analysis.
1| 901704 Engineering Contract Management
1| This course provides an overview of different contracts’ types for different project delivery
1| methods, contract terms, conditions, contents, and pricing arrangements. Students will be
1| introduced to the contracting procedures, bidding and project awarding procedures, national
1| and international procurement regulations, general contracting clauses, professional ethics,
1| change orders procedures, dispute resolutions methods, schedule delay analysis, claim
1| analysis, and construction contract management.
1| 901705 Advanced Applied Statistics
1| This course includes: Advanced analytical statistical methods, hypothesis test, multiple
1| correlation and regression, T and F distributions, analysis of variance, planned comparisons
1| and post HOC comparisons, analysis of covariance, and nonparametric techniques, and
1| utilizing of SPSS statistical package.
1| 901706 Risk Management in Engineering Projects
1| This course introduces students to the principles, processes and techniques of Project Risk
1| Management. The course will focus on risk management planning, identifying risks,
1| qualitative risk analysis, quantitative analysis, tools for quantifying risk, risk response
1| planning and monitoring, and guidance in practical risk management (case studies) and legal
1| aspects. The course also prepares students to utilize software for the purposes of risk
1| management.
